title: Pixels that whisper
summary: A pixel speaks only when the light changes.

cards.text:
A still scene is silence.
Motion, or a light turning on, makes a pixel speak.

The note says where, when,
and whether it got brighter or darker.

question.prompt: A poster that never moves produces…
question.simpler: The sensor is a change detector.

question.prompt: Stuffing the events back into frames keeps the reason you used this camera.
question.why: Frames put the clock and the dense grid back.
question.simpler: Binning can be a baseline. It is not the stream.

recall.question: When does a DVS pixel stay silent?
recall.answer: When the brightness is not changing.

deeper.note: Lichtsteiner, Posch, and Delbrück’s 2008 sensor is the 128 by 128 chip in the paper title. The later map of the field is Gallego and colleagues’ survey.

paper.title: A 128×128 120 dB 15 μs Latency Asynchronous Temporal Contrast Vision Sensor
paper.section: The pixel: temporal contrast, ON and OFF events.

terms.plain: a pixel that speaks only when light changes
terms.definition: A sensor whose output is a stream of change events, not frames.
